title: Check the remote binary is owned by the user and not other-writable before exec
description:
Security, hardening a predictable exec path. ssh.rs prelude execs $HOME/.local/share/acs/<version>/acs whenever it is executable, and install.rs creates that directory with a bare mkdir -p under the remote umask. Nothing verifies the directory or the binary is owned by the user and not group- or other-writable.

On a host where $HOME or ~/.local/share is group-writable (umask 002 with a shared group, a common lab or edge-device setup) another local user plants a binary at that exact path and every later `acs <host>` execs it as the victim. It is the generic writable-home problem, but acs adds a predictable, always-exec'd path and never checks it.

Done when the prelude refuses a candidate whose directory or file is not owned by the user or is writable by group or other, falling back to the install path with a clear message, and a test covers a loosened directory.
close_reason: Implemented in #132: the prelude checks ownership and writability before exec

title: A network hint is committed then dropped where the caller cannot act on it
description:
`NetWatch::changed()` commits the new network set (`*held = now`) and returns
true. Two callers then drop that answer:

- `serve()` discards it when `!welcomed` — a change during the handshake, which
  acs-xo1 covers as a feature gap;
- `offline()` discards it when `EARLY_EVERY` says the last early redial was too
  recent.

Either way the hint is **consumed**. The next identical hint answers "not a
change", because the set it would compare against has already moved. So the
change is not deferred, it is lost, and the only thing that recovers it is a
covering deadline — the dial timeout in the first case, the backoff in the
second.

Both sites are deliberate and their comments say so, and both are covered
today. This is filed because it is the **only** way a hint can be lost, and
that makes it the standing suspect whenever something that should have reacted
to a network change did not. acs-ryz hit exactly that shape: its one
unreproducible failure was `a_network_change_ends_a_frozen_link_without_the_dead_timeout`,
seen once and then not again in 40 isolated plus 24 full-binary runs. That pass
deliberately did **not** add a repeat-the-hint loop to the test, on the correct
reasoning that a repeat would answer "not a change" and so would only have
looked like a fix — which is itself the evidence that this shape is reachable.

The fix is probably to commit the set only where the answer is acted on, or to
carry an explicit "pending change" the next poll can re-offer. Both are small;
the care needed is in not re-introducing the storm acs-6p8 fixed, where every
route message triggered a redial.

Note the interaction: `EARLY_EVERY` exists to stop a flapping interface
redialling repeatedly, and deferring rather than dropping must not undo that —
a change deferred past the flap should collapse into one redial, not queue
several.

Done when a hint the caller could not act on is either not committed or is
re-offered on the next poll, a test drives the drop path directly (both the
handshake and the EARLY_EVERY case), a flapping interface still produces one
redial rather than several, and the comments at both sites say what now
happens.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #199 (491c637): changed() returns Option<Change<'_>> and Change::acted() commits the set, so a hint the caller could not use is offered again. #[must_use] puts the danger at the site that acts. A flap is still one redial, by construction

title: Check e2e_ssh.sh's inputs beyond the source stamp: a missing client binary and a partial dist
description:
acs-gb4 (PR #170, 2d0a719) made `scripts/e2e_ssh.sh --no-build` refuse a
`dist/` that was not built from the current tree, by comparing a content hash
written to `dist/source.stamp`. Three smaller input checks around it were left
alone; none is urgent and all three are the same shape — a bad input that
surfaces later as a confusing test failure rather than immediately as a clear
message.

**1. The client binary is never checked to exist.** The script sets
`ACS_E2E_CLIENT="$root/$client"` and lets `cargo test` fail later with whatever
the harness says about a missing file. The stamp catches the common case — no
`dist/` at all means no stamp, which is a mismatch and a refusal — but a
`dist/` built with `--targets` that omits the host's target passes the stamp
check and then fails obscurely.

**2. `cargo xtask dist --targets …` writes a full-tree stamp for a partial
dist.** The stamp says "built from this tree", which is true, and says nothing
about *which* targets were built — which is how case 1 gets through. If partial
dists ever become routine, the stamp should record the target list too. Doing 1
properly may well be enough on its own; decide whether 2 is worth it or whether
it is speculative.

**3. `--allow-stale-dist` without `--no-build` is silently ignored**, because
the build path wins. Harmless and documented in the usage line, but a usage
error would be more honest than a flag that does nothing.

Done when a missing or wrong-target client binary is refused with a message
naming the file and how to get it, the `--allow-stale-dist`-without-`--no-build`
case is decided (error or documented no-op), and whichever of these gets a
check also gets a test in `tests/scripts.rs` beside the acs-gb4 one.
notes:
Friction worth folding in, from acs-br2 (PR #208): **`scripts/e2e_ssh.sh
--no-build` cannot be used from a fresh worktree.** `dist/` does not exist
there, so the stamp check refuses and the first e2e run in any new worktree
pays a full `cargo xtask dist` (~45s of cross-building four targets).

That is correct behaviour — acs-gb4 built the refusal deliberately, and a
missing `dist/` really is a mismatch — but it is the common case for this
repo's workflow, where nearly all work happens in a fresh worktree. Every
agent-driven pass this run hit it.

It fits this bead because it is the same question: what should `--no-build` do
about an input it cannot use? The answer for a *stale* dist is "refuse". The
answer for an *absent* one might reasonably be "build it anyway and say so",
which is what the person meant, rather than an error they must then work
around.

Worth considering alongside this bead's other items whether the volume/target
directory could be shared across worktrees of the same repo, which would remove
the cost rather than the message.
close_reason: Done in PR #220 (d1aa5ac): absent is not stale — --no-build builds once when there is no dist/ at all and says so, while a dist/ that exists must still vouch for itself, including the unstamped case. Client binary checked before docker starts; --allow-stale-dist without --no-build is now a usage error

title: Emit a newline before the ACS-READY/ACS-NEED marker so printf noise cannot swallow it
description:
`parse_marker` (src/proto.rs ~L636) requires the marker to start a line. A `printf "foo"` (no `\n`) in a startup file makes the line `fooACS-READY 1` / `fooACS-NEED ...`, which is rejected. For ACS-NEED the client reports "the connection closed before acs started"; for ACS-READY the client blocks in `dial` waiting for a marker while the proxy blocks waiting for HELLO — a mutual hang with no timeout on either side (see the dial-deadline bead).

Done when `ready_line()` and the prelude's `printf` (src/ssh.rs) emit a leading `\n`, with a scanner test for noise without a trailing newline.
close_reason: Fixed with regression tests (bugs-install branch)

title: Do not Debug-format a rejected frame into an ERROR that can exceed MAX_FRAME
description: Found in review. proxy.rs:225 and :266, master.rs:765: `format!("expected HELLO..., got {other:?}")` where other may be an INPUT or DATA frame of up to 1 MiB. Vec<u8> Debug is 3-5 chars per byte, so the ERROR frame (not chunked) is several MiB and the client's decoder reports TooLarge ('bad frame') instead of the intended BAD_REQUEST text. Only a misbehaving client triggers it. Done when the message names the frame type (or a truncated safe::display) rather than the payload, with a test sending a 1 MiB INPUT before HELLO and asserting a readable ERROR.
close_reason: Fixed in #277 (1f95f5b): refused-frame ERRORs and the master log name the frame type via Msg::kind()

title: The system-wide install path now works, but nothing dials into it and nothing prunes it
description:
acs-6w9 (PR #190, ae86191) made `/usr/local/lib/acs/<version>/acs` genuinely
usable: an administrator populates it as root and every user's prelude will now
execute it. That closed the bug. It also turned a dead code path into a live
one, and two things that did not matter while it was dead now do.

**1. No end-to-end coverage.** `scripts/e2e_ssh.sh` only ever exercises the
`$HOME` candidate. The system candidate is covered by prelude unit tests and by
`tests/multiuser.rs` running the prelude directly as root — good coverage of the
*decision*, none of the *path*. Nothing dials a real ssh connection into a host
where **only** `/usr/local/lib/acs/<v>/acs` exists and confirms a session comes
up on it without a first-contact install. That is the scenario an administrator
who sets this up is actually buying, and it is the one thing untested.

The e2e container is the natural place: a variant host with the binary installed
system-wide and `$HOME` empty. Worth checking what `acs _install` does if it
finds the system copy already good — it should not install a second one.

**2. Nobody prunes it.** `src/prune.rs` correctly never touches
`/usr/local/lib/acs` — it is not ours to delete, and a user cannot remove root's
files anyway. But now that versions accumulate there for real, there is no
documented story for who reclaims a stale one. An administrator who populates it
once per release, as DESIGN §8 suggests, gets a directory that grows forever with
nothing saying so.

This does not need code: it may be a paragraph in DESIGN §8 telling the
administrator that pruning the system path is theirs to do, and perhaps a line
in `acs prune`'s output noting a system version it can see but will not remove.
Decide which, rather than leaving it unsaid.

Done when a real ssh dial into a host carrying only the system-wide install
attaches without installing anything, and DESIGN §8 says who is responsible for
removing old versions from the system path — with `acs prune` mentioning what it
deliberately leaves alone if that is the chosen answer.
close_reason: Done in #304 (66a2175): e2e_16 dials a host whose only acs is the system-wide install and asserts no install and no second copy; DESIGN §8 says pruning /usr/local/lib/acs is the administrator's job (docs only, no code).

title: Chmod the payload-path binary to 0755 explicitly instead of relying on the umask
description:
install::write_exe (src/install.rs:282-294) relies on OpenOptions::mode(0o755), which the remote umask masks (umask 077 gives 0700), whereas the self-copy path (install.rs:126) does an explicit chmod 755. Only matters if the per-user directory is ever shared, but the two paths disagree and tests/install.rs asserts 0755 only on the self-copy path.

Done when write_exe sets the mode after writing and the install test asserts 0755 on the payload path under a restrictive umask.
close_reason: Implemented in #95 (eeb5969)

title: Timing windows in the files acs-ryz did not reach, and a diagnostic that cannot explain itself
description:
acs-ryz (PRs #194, 50fc179 and #195, 3ce7f21) cleared the reconnect, alias and
master suites. Three windows of the same class sit in files it did not reach,
plus one diagnostic gap that made its single unexplained failure unexplainable.

**The windows:**

- `host_aliases::a_host_slower_than_the_deadline_is_passed_over` — two: the
  fallback host's ping must answer inside the alias's own 5 s, and
  `took < 25 s` is an upper bound on elapsed time. 8 failures of 63 at extreme
  load.
- `client::resize_reaches_the_program` — a 200 ms settle between `resize()` and
  the `\r`. Exactly acs-7wu's shape. It also went red once during acs-ryz
  (`timed out waiting "ready"`) and passed alone.
- `alias::tests::ping_is_killed_at_the_deadline` — `start.elapsed() < 800ms`,
  an upper bound a loaded host can break.

Upper bounds are the harder half: a lower bound is safe under contention
(starving the machine only makes the event later), an upper bound is exactly
what contention breaks. Where the assertion really is about elapsed time,
acs-cu8's move applies — keep it, widen the slack until it is out of reach of
realistic load. Where it is standing in for "this did not fall back to the slow
path", it should say that instead.

**The diagnostic gap:** `assert_consecutive` / `numbers()` in
`tests/reconnect.rs` cannot distinguish a **torn** number from **lost** output.
acs-ryz's one unexplained burst reported `lost or repeated output around
174 → 17`, where the `17` looks like half of a `175` split mid-write rather
than a gap in the stream. As written, the helper turns a display bug into what
looks like a protocol bug, and the next person will chase the wrong thing.
Printing the surrounding bytes on failure would settle it in one run.
acs-z22 — a `-v` note on fd 2 splitting a frame on fd 1 — is the obvious
suspect, and that connection can only be made if the bytes are visible.

Done when none of the three windows can be lost to realistic load, each still
goes red for what it covers (show it), and `assert_consecutive` prints enough
of the surrounding stream on failure to tell a torn write from a lost one.
notes:
**acs-z22 (PR #201, da1368c) does NOT close the torn-vs-lost half of this
bead**, and that pass was explicit about it so nobody reads #201 as having
fixed it.

A boundary there means "not inside an escape sequence, an OSC/DCS string, or a
multi-byte UTF-8 character". `#175#` is plain ASCII, so **every** byte position
in it is a boundary — a note raised while the stream sits between `#17` and
`5#` still goes out there, and `numbers()` still sees `17` where `175` was.
acs-z22 removed escape-sequence and UTF-8 tearing, not line tearing. Holding
notes to a newline instead would mean holding them indefinitely in a
full-screen program, which is worse than the disease.

So the fix stays on the test side, and that pass suggested the shape: teach
`numbers()` to **stitch across an `acs: …` line** the way it already stitches
across the status line's `ESC 7 … ESC 8` span. That turns the `174 → 17`
mystery into a parse detail rather than a reported protocol failure, which is
what this bead's diagnostic half is asking for.

Two more for the timing half of this bead, both in `tests/client.rs`:

- `single_escape_press_and_other_keys_reach_the_program` — two fixed sleeps
  gating an `od -N 4` read. Timed out twice under full-parallel macOS load
  during acs-z22 (`timed out waiting for "armed"` — the program's *first* byte
  never arrived), 12/12 green alone. Not acs-br2, and not acs-z22's doing: that
  test runs no `-v`, so the changed path is never taken.
- The empty-output shape already noted here has now been seen in a fourth test
  in that file, which strengthens the case that `tests/client.rs` has a startup
  problem rather than a slowness problem.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #205 (661e1dc): three windows removed or turned into lower bounds, and numbers()/assert_consecutive moved to tests/common and taught to stitch across a note plus drop a trailing torn fragment. CORRECTION: the empty-output shape is slowness, not a startup stall — 86 failures at T=30s became 6 at T=300s, and 850/850 green with the I/O pressure removed; five survivors were clients SIGKILLed externally. No product bug

title: Package acs for Homebrew with a tap updated on release
description:
Package acs for distribution with Homebrew.

User's ask: "package the application for distribution with Homebrew".

Today acs ships as GitHub release archives (acs-<version>-<target>.tar.gz for macOS arm64/x86_64 and Linux x86_64/aarch64, plus SHA256SUMS), the one-line installer, and `acs upgrade` (docs/VERSIONING.md, scripts/release-binaries.sh).

Proposed shape:

- A tap repository, `michel-onstein/homebrew-acs`, with `Formula/acs.rb` that installs the prebuilt release archive for the machine (on_macos/on_linux, on_arm/on_intel), with its sha256 from SHA256SUMS. `brew install michel-onstein/acs/acs`. A prebuilt binary keeps the complete build with its Linux payloads (DESIGN §8.1); building from source would give a slim build that cannot install other platforms' remotes.
- The formula is updated by the release: scripts/release-binaries.sh (or `cargo xtask`) rewrites version, URLs and sha256s and pushes to the tap after publishing.
- `brew test`: `acs --version` reports the version.
- A Homebrew-installed acs should not replace itself: `acs upgrade` detects it runs from a Homebrew Cellar path and says `brew upgrade acs`, and the weekly update-check message suggests the same.
- README "Install" lists `brew install`.

Done when `brew install michel-onstein/acs/acs` installs the current release on macOS (and Linuxbrew), `brew test acs` passes, a release updates the formula automatically, and `acs upgrade` defers to brew for a brewed install.
close_reason: Implemented with tests: tap michel-onstein/homebrew-acs, formula rendered and pushed on release, acs upgrade defers to brew (PR #27)

title: Warn when the latest release reported is older than the last one seen
description:
Security, update freeze. upgrade::decide correctly refuses to install an older release unless --version pins it, so a straight rollback is blocked. But an attacker controlling the channel, or a stale mirror, can serve an old but genuine SHA256SUMS indefinitely: decide reports nothing to do, the weekly check stays silent, and the user sits on a vulnerable version with no signal. There is no freshness or expiry metadata.

update_check's State already persists the last latest it saw, so the comparison is nearly free.

Done when a reported latest older than the stored one produces a visible warning rather than silence, the stored value is not overwritten by the older one, and a test covers the regression.
close_reason: Implemented in #134: a channel offering an older release is reported once

title: Refuse or skip the local config when $HOME is unset instead of using a CWD-relative path
description: Found in review and reproduced: `env -u HOME -u XDG_CONFIG_HOME acs config path` prints `local:  .config/acs/config.yaml`. config::local_path (config.rs:251-260) does var_os("HOME").unwrap_or_default() and joins .config onto an empty PathBuf, so acs config set would create_dir_all(./.config/acs) in whatever directory the user is in, and the client reads a different config per CWD. install.rs:406 already refuses with 'HOME is not set'. Done when local_path refuses (or yields None and the local file is skipped) with HOME unset, and a test covers it.
close_reason: Fixed in #246 (c124b69): local_file() is None without an absolute HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME; client skips the local file, acs config refuses

title: Give a Pending connection a deadline so a childless master cannot be kept alive forever
description: Found in review. master.rs:426-433: the 30 s 'no client ever created the session' exit requires self.conns.is_empty(), and liveness (c.live.tick, line 456) runs only for Active connections. A Pending connection that never sends a HELLO (a stuck or hostile same-uid process) keeps a childless master alive indefinitely, and status/list keep showing it. Done when a Pending connection that has not completed HELLO within a bound is dropped (or Pending connections do not count against the 30 s rule), with a test connecting silently and asserting the master exits.
close_reason: Fixed in #258 (4d0fa1e)

title: Add a curl | sh installer for acs (per-platform install dir)
description:
Add a one-line installer: `curl -fsSL <url> | sh` installs acs the way the platform expects.

User's ask: "create an install script that someone can download which installs acs automatically according to the rules of the platform it is being installed on. Similar to other apps: `curl <something> | <some shell command>`."

Proposed design:

- `scripts/install.sh`, POSIX sh. It is also published as a release asset by `scripts/release-binaries.sh`, so the stable URL is `https://github.com/michel-onstein/acs/releases/latest/download/install.sh`. The repo is public.
- It maps `uname -s` / `uname -m` to one of the four release targets: macOS arm64/x86_64, Linux x86_64/aarch64. Anything else is a clear error.
- It downloads `acs-<version>-<target>.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS` from the release (latest by default; `ACS_VERSION=0.2.0` pins one) and refuses to install on a checksum mismatch. It uses `curl` or `wget`, and `shasum -a 256` or `sha256sum`.
- Install location follows each platform's rules: per-user `~/.local/bin` (XDG) by default, or `/usr/local/bin` when run as root or with `ACS_INSTALL_DIR`. It warns, with the line to add, when the directory is not on `PATH`.
- Re-running it upgrades in place, and it prints the installed `acs --version`.

Today install is manual: README "Install" has a curl + tar + install recipe, and the release assets exist since v0.1.0.

Done when: the script passes shellcheck; tests run it against a real release in Alpine and Ubuntu containers and in a temp HOME on macOS (default dir, pinned version, checksum failure, unsupported platform); README leads with the one-liner.
close_reason: Implemented: scripts/install.sh (curl|sh, wget fallback, SHA256SUMS check, versioned layout ~/.local or /usr/local, ACS_VERSION/ACS_INSTALL_DIR), published as a release asset; scripts/test_install.sh passes on macOS, Alpine and Ubuntu as root and user

title: CLAUDE.md says the version is bumped by a ship workflow, and two agents have read that as CI
description:
`CLAUDE.md:27` says the version moves automatically after every merge to `main`,
"`scripts/version-bump.sh`, run by the ship workflow".

There is **no `.github/` in this repo at all** — `git ls-files .github` is empty,
so there are no GitHub Actions, no checks on any PR, and nothing that runs the
script on a schedule or a trigger. What actually runs it is the **`ship` skill**,
at its own step 9, on the machine of whoever is landing the change.

That reading is almost certainly what "the ship workflow" means, and the
sentence is not false. But it has now misled **two independent agents** working
this repo, both of whom stopped to check whether CI was broken or a workflow had
gone missing — one concluding the doc was stale, the other concluding it was
fine. When two careful readers reach opposite conclusions from one sentence, the
sentence is the problem.

The cost is small but recurring: every new contributor or agent who notices
`gh pr checks` saying "no checks reported" has to work out from scratch whether
that is expected. It is.

Two things worth saying explicitly wherever this is reworded:

- **the version bump is a local step, not an automated one** — if nobody runs
  `ship`, or ship is told to skip step 9, `main` simply sits ahead of its last
  tag until someone bumps;
- **there is no CI**, deliberately or not. `scripts/verify.sh` is the gate and it
  runs where the person runs it. That is a fact worth stating once rather than
  rediscovering, and it is the reason every pass in this repo has to run the
  suites by hand.

Note this repo's own "status is part of the change" rule is the argument for
fixing it: a doc that reads as describing automation that does not exist is the
same failure mode that rule exists to prevent, just in the tooling rather than
the feature set.

Done when CLAUDE.md says who runs the bump and when, and says plainly that the
repo has no CI, so that "no checks reported" needs no investigation.
close_reason: Landed in #294 (f546a10): CLAUDE.md and VERSIONING.md say there is no CI, verify.sh is the local gate, and the bump is a local ship step

title: Create the upgrade and update-check scratch directories 0700
description: Found in review. upgrade.rs:248-249 (Scratch::new) and update_check.rs:210-211 create the scratch directory under temp_dir() with std::fs::create_dir, i.e. 0777 & ~umask; sys::Umask exists but is not used. Everything after is by path: release.rs:355 verifies SHA256SUMS then :356 re-reads it; upgrade.rs:357-358 reads and hashes the archive, then :365 hands the path to tar, then Staged::new copies the extracted acs by path (:425). A user with umask 002 and a shared primary group (the scenario DESIGN 8.1 / acs-08m take seriously) gets a group-writable /tmp/acs-upgrade.<token>; a group member who races the swap between read and tar, or between verify and re-read, gets their binary run by check_runs and installed. Not reachable under sudo (root's umask is normally 022). scripts/install.sh:115 gets this right (mktemp -d, 0700). Done when both directories are created 0700 (DirBuilderExt::mode or Umask::set(0o077) around the create), which closes every by-path step at once, with a test asserting the mode under umask 002.
close_reason: Fixed in #259: upgrade::scratch_dir creates both scratch directories 0700; regression tests under umask 002

title: Derive the test suite's outlasting timers from T, so the deadline can move
description: acs-hsw kept testutil::T at 30 s partly because it is not a free lever: tests prove 'only X can have happened' by waiting at most T against timers hard-coded to outlast it — ACS_DEAD_MS 60000 for the master, reachability_timeout: 60s (tests/common/mod.rs Net::env), the silenced host's exec sleep 60, ACS_BACKOFF_MS / ACS_EARLY_MS / ACS_REDIAL_TIMEOUT_MS 120000 with their 'reconnecting in 120s' expectations (tests/reconnect.rs), ACS_ESCAPE_TIMEOUT_MS 30000/60000, and the prose that says 'two minutes, four times T'. Express those as multiples of T (constants in testutil or tests/common), so a later decision to raise T (e.g. to the client's 120 s first-dial timeout) is one edit, and the unit test the_deadline_stays_under_half_the_suites_minute_timers becomes a relation between constants rather than against a literal minute. Done when every such timer in tests/ is derived from T and the suite is green.
close_reason: Landed in #395 (7eb3652): outlasting timers derived from testutil::T

title: The real PF_ROUTE and netlink watcher has no end-to-end test, and now carries more weight
description:
acs-6p8 (PR #180, f196120) made a kernel hint insufficient on its own: a redial
happens only when `netmatch::local_networks()` shows the machine's own networks
actually moved. That is the right contract, and it puts more weight on a path
nothing tests end to end.

What is covered today:

- `platform_watcher_opens` — the socket opens.
- `route_messages_matter` — the byte filter accepts the right message types.
- the new unit and integration tests — the *decision*, driven through
  `ACS_NETWATCH_FIFO` and `ACS_NETWATCH_NETS`.

What is not covered anywhere: that a **real** roam, wake or VPN transition on
macOS `PF_ROUTE` or Linux netlink actually emits a message the filter accepts
**and** moves an address that `local_networks()` reports. Both halves have to
be true for the feature to work, and both are assumptions about the platform
rather than about acs. If a macOS release changed which messages accompany a
Wi-Fi roam, or if a VPN came up without moving any address `LocalNet::usable`
accepts, the feature would go quietly dead: no error, no log, just a session
that waits out the backoff instead of redialling at once.

The acs-6p8 pass wrote this into `docs/VERIFICATION.md` as a by-hand item, which
is the honest short-term answer. This bead is about whether it can stop being
by hand.

Hard part, and why it is P3 rather than P2: the test needs the machine's real
network to change, which CI cannot do and a developer will not do casually.
Options to weigh — a Linux container where an interface can genuinely be
created, addressed and torn down (netns makes this cheap and would cover the
netlink half properly); a macOS test gated behind an env var that a person sets
when they are about to roam; or accepting it stays by hand and instead logging
loudly under `-v` when a hint arrives and is judged not-a-change, so the silent
failure at least leaves a trace.

Done when either the platform half is exercised automatically on at least one
platform — a real interface change, not an injected file — or the decision not
to is recorded with the `-v` trace that makes a quietly dead watcher visible,
and VERIFICATION.md's by-hand item reflects whichever way it went.
notes:
Re-weighted P3 to P2 after acs-ft1 (PR #182, ecd5d5e).

The untested platform path is now load-bearing twice over. acs-6p8 made it
decide whether an offline wait is cut short; acs-ft1 makes it decide whether a
*connected, healthy* session is probed and, if the host does not answer within
ACS_NETCHECK_MS, declared dead at ~2s instead of ~10s.

So a watcher that quietly stopped emitting — a macOS release changing which
messages accompany a roam, a VPN that comes up without moving an address
LocalNet::usable accepts — no longer merely delays a redial. It silently
removes the mechanism that makes a wake-from-sleep or a Wi-Fi switch recover
in 1-2s, and there is nothing in the logs to say so: the absence of a hint
looks exactly like a network that did not change.

That is the argument for the `-v` trace option in the description. Even if the
platform half stays a by-hand check, a line when a hint arrives and is judged
not-a-change would distinguish "the watcher is working and nothing moved" from
"the watcher is dead", which today are indistinguishable from outside.
close_reason: Done in PR #192 (9bc0b5c), both outcomes: tests/netns.rs drives the real kernel via ip link/addr under CAP_NET_ADMIN in test_linux.sh, shown red two ways; and a -v trace makes a dead watcher visible on macOS, where silence across a roam is now evidence

title: Verify the uploaded binary on the remote before executing it
description:
Security, self-attested integrity. The remote install script is `set -e; mkdir -p <dir>; cat > <tmp>; chmod 755 <tmp>; exec <tmp> _install --finish --token <t> --sha256 <digest>` (install.rs). Verified by reading it: the uploaded file is made executable and RUN, and the digest the client computed is then checked by the very binary being checked, which hashes its own current_exe(). A substituted binary simply skips the check and prints ok, which is all side_call looks for. In the payload path the appended blob is only structurally parsed by Payloads::parse and never checksummed.

Attack: anyone who can replace the file between the cat and the exec (a second person on a shared account, a compromised sshd, a remote whose $HOME is writable by others) gets their code run and then installed at ~/.local/share/acs/<v>/acs, which every later acs connection execs.

Already good, so do not redo it: the token is 64 bits from /dev/urandom, write_exe uses create_new (O_EXCL), and parse_finish rejects a non-hex token.

Done when the client verifies the digest before the binary is executed (a shasum/sha256sum call on the remote, or reading the file back) and the payload blob is digested too, with a test that a tampered upload is refused.
close_reason: Implemented in #113: the remote shell checks the digest before the upload can run

title: Ping IPv6 alias hosts on macOS, where ping is IPv4-only
description:
alias::ping_with (src/alias.rs:237-252) runs the system ping and takes status.success() as reachable. macOS ping is IPv4-only: `ping -c 1 -t 2 -- ::1` exits 68 "cannot resolve", so an IPv6 literal or a name with only AAAA records can never be chosen.

Scenario: aliases: nas: [{host: "fd00:1::20"}] or an IPv6-only LAN name. With -v acs logs "does not answer ping within 500ms" every time and exits 255, or falls back to the wrong entry, although ssh would connect fine. prefer_local_network explicitly matches IPv6 networks (README, netmatch tests with fd00:1::5/64), so a user on an IPv6 LAN sees "is on the local network fd00:1::/64" followed by "does not answer ping". Linux iputils ping is dual-stack, so this is macOS-specific.

Done when an IPv6 literal (or a ping exit 68 on macOS) uses ping6, or the README documents reachability_check: false for such hosts, with a test for the IPv6 literal path.
close_reason: Implemented in #79 (1fea487)

title: Carry a half-read frame over the proxy's HELLO hand-off to the relay
description:
proxy::attach (src/proxy.rs:280-285) re-encodes only complete frames left in dec (`while let Ok(Some(m)) = dec.next_msg()`); bytes of an incomplete frame (dec.pending() > 0) are discarded, and relay_fds then reads fresh from stdin, forwarding the remainder of that frame to the master with its head missing. The master's decoder desyncs, answers BAD_REQUEST/Closing, and the client exits with code::ERROR.

Latent today: the client sends nothing between HELLO and WELCOME (stdin and SIGWINCH are gated on welcomed, client.rs:885-903). Any future pipelining after HELLO (e.g. sending the unacked resend with the HELLO) would hit it. Decoder::take_rest() exists for exactly this and pick.rs uses it.

Done when attach appends dec.take_rest() to the bytes forwarded to the master, with a proxy test that splits a RESIZE across the hand-off.
close_reason: Implemented in #97 (4996762)

title: Bound the key lexer string state so command mode cannot be suppressed
description:
Security, denial of the detach key. keys.rs enters Lex::Str on ESC ] , ESC P or ESC _ from stdin and then forwards every byte raw without calling token(), so Ctrl-] is not recognised, command mode cannot arm and Detach cannot fire. The only way out is the 100 ms idle timeout in tick, which never fires while bytes keep arriving.

Attack: a malicious remote sets a multi-megabyte clipboard with OSC 52 and queries it back in a loop. The terminal streams one enormous continuously-arriving reply, the user's Ctrl-] Ctrl-] d is swallowed into it and forwarded to the attacker instead, and the session cannot be detached without killing the terminal. DESIGN §6.3 documents the timeout as the mitigation for the Alt+_ case only; the adversarial case is not considered.

Related to the already-filed Alt+_ lexer bug, which is the accidental version of the same state.

Done when the string state is bounded by total bytes as well as idle time, the command key is recognised even inside it (or the state is abandoned on a cap), and a test streams an unending OSC reply and still detaches.
close_reason: Implemented in #121: the string state is bounded by bytes as well as by silence

title: Let a fork set at build time which repo updates come from
description:
User's words: "is it possible at release time to specify which github repo updates are coming from? This is needed in case someone wants to fork".

Today it is not. The update source can only be changed at **runtime, per environment**, never baked into the binary a fork ships.

Verified (v0.11.4):

- `release::DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL` (src/release.rs:16) is a plain hardcoded const, `https://github.com/michel-onstein/acs/releases`.
- `release::releases_url()` (src/release.rs:35) lets `ACS_RELEASES_URL` override it, and that is honoured by `acs upgrade` (upgrade.rs:273) and the weekly update check (update_check.rs:220), and separately by scripts/install.sh:25-26. The guards from acs-95w stay as they are: https only unless `--allow-insecure-url` is passed on the command line, and ignored outright when the real and effective uid differ.
- There is no config-file setting for it: `local_networks` and friends are in `config::KEYS`, a releases URL is not.
- `build.rs` already emits `cargo:rustc-env=ACS_TARGET`, so the compile-time mechanism needed here is in place and used.

So a fork has two bad options: patch the const (a merge conflict on every upstream sync) or tell every one of its users to export `ACS_RELEASES_URL` forever.

Change: let the default be chosen at build time, falling back to today's constant.

```rust
// build.rs
println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=ACS_DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL");
if let Ok(u) = std::env::var("ACS_DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL") {
    println!("cargo:rustc-env=ACS_DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL={u}");
}

// src/release.rs
pub const DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL: &str = match option_env!("ACS_DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL") {
    Some(u) => u,
    None => "https://github.com/michel-onstein/acs/releases",
};
```

This is not a loosening of acs-95w. The runtime guards exist because the environment is attacker-controllable across a privilege boundary; a compiled-in value is chosen by whoever builds the binary, who already decides what it does. The sudo and https rules on the runtime override are untouched.

The other places a fork must still change, which this bead should cover or explicitly leave out:

| Where | What | Overridable today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| src/release.rs:16 | update check, `acs upgrade` | env only |
| src/install.rs:85 `INSTALLER` | the `curl ... \| sh` line in the "not installed" message (install.rs:96) | no, hardcoded |
| scripts/install.sh:25 | the installer's own default | `ACS_RELEASES_URL` |
| xtask/src/formula.rs:9 `REPO` | Homebrew formula URLs | no |
| xtask/src/package.rs:31,35 | install instructions written into NOTES.md | no |
| scripts/update-tap.sh:30 | which tap to push | `ACS_TAP_REPO` (already done) |

`update-tap.sh` already anticipated this; nothing else did. `INSTALLER` is only used in a message, so it is cosmetic, but it sends a fork's users upstream to install and should derive from the same base.

Interacts with acs-o9v (sign release artifacts), which is parked on a signing-scheme decision: if a fork publishes its own releases, the key embedded in the binary has to be the fork's key too. Whatever mechanism lands here for the URL is the natural one for the key, so o9v should be designed with this in mind rather than hardcoding one key. Not a blocking dependency in either direction — they are coupled by design, not by order.

Nothing in docs/ covers forking at all: a grep for "fork" over docs/ and README.md finds only `forkpty`.

Done when the default releases URL can be set at build time and falls back to today's value when unset, `INSTALLER` derives from the same base rather than being its own const, a test covers both the unset and the set case, and a short "Forking" section in docs/VERSIONING.md lists every knob a fork must set (the build-time URL, `ACS_TAP_REPO`, the xtask formula/package strings) so the list above does not have to be rediscovered.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #153 (be220ed): ACS_DEFAULT_RELEASES_URL at build time, installer() derives from it, Forking section in VERSIONING.md

title: acs <host>'s session menu still gets an empty list, not an ERROR, when the remote cannot read its socket directory
description: Follow-up to acs-mum0 (PR #241). That fix made _proxy --list send an ERROR frame when write_statuses fails, and list.rs query() treats it as a failure. The pick path does not: proxy.rs send_list (~L436) calls write_statuses(dir, STDOUT)? and returns the error without sending Msg::Error, so the client sees EOF with no LIST_END. pick::Pick::list already records Msg::Error, so only the proxy side is missing. Done when send_list sends an ERROR frame (as list() now does) before failing, and a test makes the pick listing fail and asserts the menu shows the error rather than an empty or truncated list.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #281 (69fabda): send_list sends an ERROR when the sessions cannot be read, and the pick reports it

title: YAML edge cases: tab before #, dropped ---, dangling-symlink write, errors citing the unsaved file
description: Found in review; four small items filed as one. (1) yaml.rs:477 (also :422, :705): a tab before # is not a comment, so `a: x\t# c` parses as the value "x\t# c" and the next edit rewrites it as a: "x\t# c", cementing the comment into the value; YAML 1.2 lets tab separate the comment, the rule acs-qjx applied to `key:\tvalue`. (2) yaml.rs:197-205 drops --- and ... at parse and never re-emits them, so every edit deletes a leading --- despite the 'comments and order intact' promise; a %YAML 1.2 header gets the misleading 'line 2: only one YAML document is supported'. (3) config_cmd.rs:1111 write() through a dangling symlink: canonicalize fails when the target does not exist yet (a dotfiles link before first write), the fallback is the link path, and rename(tmp, link) replaces the symlink with a regular file, the case acs-q8e fixed minus the existing target. (4) config_cmd.rs:1105: `acs config host add nas me@h` on a 5-line file reports '...config.yaml:6: aliases.nas: host: bad host name ... (not saved; fix the file by hand)' because the line is in the unsaved emitted text; tests/config_cmd.rs:292-297 asserts only the substring. Done when each has a regression test.
close_reason: Fixed in #308 (e58bf96): tab-separated comments, ---/... markers kept, %YAML refused by name, dangling-symlink write, refused edits cite real lines

title: acs v1: single-binary persistent ssh sessions
description:
Implement `acs` as designed in `docs/DESIGN.md`: one Rust binary that is the
local client, the per-connection remote proxy and the per-session remote
master, replacing the `dsh` shell function (ssh + dtach).

Invariants every child must preserve:

- Unfiltered stream: pty bytes reach the local terminal verbatim; keystrokes
  reach the pty verbatim except the command key (DESIGN §2, §6).
- Transport is the system `ssh`; no ssh-side configuration (DESIGN §3).
- Lossless resume after a network drop (DESIGN §5.2).

Done when every child is closed and DESIGN.md's Status reads Built.
close_reason: All 25 children closed: acs v1 implemented, tested on macOS and Linux, verified end to end over real ssh

title: Scaffold the acs crate: size-tuned profile, role dispatch, verify script
description:
Create the Cargo project the rest of the plan builds on (DESIGN §9).

- `Cargo.toml`: release profile `opt-level = "z"`, `lto = true`,
  `codegen-units = 1`, `panic = "abort"`, `strip = true`. Dependencies kept
  minimal: `rustix` (or `nix`) and `lexopt`; no async runtime, no clap.
- `src/main.rs`: role dispatch — default client; hidden `_proxy`, `_master`,
  `_install`, `_version`. Stubs are fine.
- Module skeleton per DESIGN §9 layout (`proto.rs`, `client/`, `master/`,
  `proxy.rs`, `install.rs`) and an `xtask/` workspace member placeholder.
- `scripts/verify.sh`: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`,
  `cargo test`, `npx markdownlint-cli2` on `**/*.md`.
- Flip DESIGN.md `Status:` to "In progress" and its CLAUDE.md index row, in
  the same change (repo convention).

Acceptance: `scripts/verify.sh` passes; `cargo zigbuild --release --target
x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` build; the slim
binary size for each target is recorded in the PR/commit message as the
baseline against the < 1 MB budget.

title: Master: session protocol, takeover, resume, resize, kill
description:
The master's side of the protocol (DESIGN §4.2, §5.2, §5.3).

- HELLO handling with attach / create / attach-or-create; WELCOME with
  instance id and resumed / gap / fresh.
- One active client: a new attach sends TAKEOVER to the previous one.
- Output: pty reads go into the ring; DATA frames from the client's offset;
  backpressure while attached (stop reading the pty when unsent bytes would
  be overwritten); ring wraps freely while detached.
- Input: INPUT dedupe by seq, ACK.
- RESIZE via `TIOCSWINSZ`; on a fresh attach force a redraw by signalling
  `tcgetpgrp(pty)` with SIGWINCH even when the size is unchanged.
- PING/PONG; DETACH; KILL = SIGHUP to the child's process group, SIGKILL
  after 3 s; EXIT{status} to the client on child exit.

Tests (framed test client over the unix socket): resume from an offset
yields exactly the missed bytes; offset beyond the ring yields gap; a new
instance yields fresh; takeover; KILL kills a process group that ignores
SIGHUP; backpressure engages with a stalled client and not when detached.
close_reason: Master protocol verified by 10 integration tests: exact resume replay, gap and fresh attach, same-identity silent takeover vs BUSY + force, KILL SIGHUP then SIGKILL after 3s, backpressure for a stalled client and none while detached, resize, forced redraw on fresh attach, input dedupe

title: Proxy: connect-or-spawn master and relay frames
description:
`acs _proxy <session> <mode> --proto N` (DESIGN §3, §4.3).

- Resolve the socket directory; connect; on ENOENT/ECONNREFUSED unlink a
  stale socket and start the master (create modes only), waiting for its
  readiness report.
- Write `ACS-READY <proto>` to stdout before the first frame.
- Check the protocol version in the client's HELLO; on mismatch answer
  ERROR telling the user to finish or kill the session.
- Splice stdin/stdout <-> socket until either side closes.

Tests: stale socket replaced; two proxies racing to create converge on one
master; mismatched protocol version yields ERROR.
close_reason: proxy.rs: connect-or-start (retries when another master wins), ACS-READY, HELLO proto check, --new naming under dir lock, splice relay, --list; 7 integration tests via stdio incl. stale socket, racing proxies, mismatch, missing session, --new numbering, dropped client detaches

title: Session listing (--list) via STATUS
description:
`acs <host> --list` (DESIGN §4.3, §4.5).

- Master answers STATUS with name, attached/detached, attached identity (or
  last attached), creator identity, created-at, idle time, child command,
  size, acs version.
- `acs _proxy --list` enumerates `<dir>/*.sock`, queries each, reports and
  removes stale sockets; no `ps` parsing.
- Client prints an aligned table; `no sessions` when empty.

Tests: listing with attached, detached and stale sessions; output format.
close_reason: list.rs: side call to _proxy --list, STATUS_REPLY frames rendered as NAME/STATE/WHO/IDLE/AGE/COMMAND table, 'no sessions', not-installed case; tests: unit table + integration with attached, detached and stale socket

title: Client terminal: raw mode, guaranteed restore, signals
description:
Local tty handling (DESIGN §7).

- Raw mode with dtach's termios flags; the original termios restored on
  every exit path: normal return, SIGHUP/SIGTERM/SIGINT, and panic (drop
  guard plus signal handler, `panic = "abort"`).
- Self-pipe for signals; SIGWINCH surfaced as a resize event.
- Single-threaded `poll` loop skeleton with timers (escape timeout, pings).

Tests: termios flag computation as a unit test; a pty-based test that the
terminal is restored after the client is killed by a signal and after a
panic.
close_reason: tty.rs RawMode (dtach flags, suspend/resume) + emergency restore via panic hook and SIGTERM/HUP/QUIT/INT handlers; sys.rs termios/pty/poll/pipe/signal self-pipe/peer_uid/wait wrappers; pty-based tests prove restore after SIGTERM and after panic

title: Integration test harness: local transport, pty runner, producers
description:
Shared test infrastructure for everything end-to-end (DESIGN §9.1).

- Temp `ACS_SOCKET_DIR` and temp `HOME` per test.
- Run the client under a pty with `--transport-cmd` pointing at the built
  binary's `_proxy` (no ssh).
- Deterministic producers (numbered lines, binary patterns incl. escape
  sequences) and a byte-exact capture of the client's stdout.
- A framed test client for driving the master/proxy directly.
- Transport killer to simulate a network drop mid-stream.

Acceptance: a smoke test attaches, runs a producer, and asserts byte
equality of output; harness usable from `cargo test`.
close_reason: tests/common: Remote fixture (temp HOME with versioned install, socket dir, pid-recording transport wrapper to cut links), pty Client runner (keys, resize, wait_for, exit code), binary pattern producer; smoke tests prove prelude->proxy->master->pty chain byte-exact and ACS-NEED

title: Client: ssh transport, handshake and byte-exact session
description:
The client's session path without reconnect (DESIGN §3, §4.4, §5, §6, §7).

- Spawn ssh via the builder; sync on `ACS-READY` (discard noise, show it
  under `-v`); detect `ACS-NEED` and hand off to install.
- HELLO with TERM, COLORTERM, size; DATA written verbatim to stdout while
  tracking the last offset; stdin through the command-key detector into
  INPUT with seq; RESIZE on SIGWINCH.
- `d`: DETACH, restore terminal (with observer resets), print
  `acs: detached from <host>/<name> - reattach with: acs <host> <name>`,
  exit 0. `x`: KILL, wait for EXIT, exit with the child's status.
- On creating a session print `acs: new session '<name>' on <host>` on
  stderr before raw mode.
- Exit codes per DESIGN §7.

Tests (harness): attach-or-create, byte-exact output incl. escape sequences,
detach and re-attach, `x` ends the remote session, EXIT status propagated,
new-session message.
close_reason: client.rs: dial with marker sync, HELLO/WELCOME, raw mode, verbatim DATA with offset tracking, detector->INPUT with seq, RESIZE, d/x, new-session and reattach messages, mode resets, exit codes; 11 pty tests incl. 300 KB byte-exact output, detach/reattach, x, exit status, single-escape passthrough

title: Client: liveness, automatic reconnect and lossless resume
description:
Resume after network drops (DESIGN §5.2-5.4).

- PING after 3 s of silence; link dead after 10 s without a frame: kill ssh
  and redial with backoff 1 s -> 30 s, reset after a connection that lasted
  30 s. `--no-reconnect` disables.
- HELLO with resume{instance, offset}; handle resumed / gap (clear + redraw)
  / fresh ("session was restarted").
- Resend unacked input; drop keys typed while the link is known down, but
  keep command mode working (`d` detaches while down; `x` reports it needs
  the link).
- Status while disconnected: nothing for < 10 s; then one bottom-row line
  with save/restore cursor and the xterm title stack; one forced redraw
  after a resume that followed a status line.
- Cooked mode while ssh authenticates on redial (password / key touch).
- TAKEOVER ends the client with a message and the reattach hint.

Tests (harness): kill the transport mid-stream and assert the client's
stdout equals the producer's output byte for byte; input sent before the
drop is not duplicated; ring overflow while disconnected yields gap
handling; `--no-reconnect` exits on drop.
close_reason: reconnect.rs: Liveness (PING after 3s, dead after 10s), Backoff 1s->30s with reset, redial with resume, unacked resend, keys dropped while down but d works and x explains, status line + title stack, redraw via resize pair; 7 pty tests (cut, freeze, input once, --no-reconnect, detach while down, x needs link, gap) + unit tests; daemons close inherited fds

title: Client: immediate redial on network change
description:
Stretch goal from DESIGN §5.3: skip the backoff wait when the default route
changes (Wi-Fi switch, wake from sleep) — route socket / SCNetworkReachability
on macOS, netlink on Linux — where it is cheap to observe.

Tests: the reconnect scheduler redials immediately on an injected
"network changed" event.
close_reason: netwatch.rs: PF_ROUTE (address/interface messages only, ARP churn ignored) on macOS, NETLINK_ROUTE link/addr groups on Linux, FIFO injection for tests; offline wait redials at once on a change (max once per 2s) and resets backoff; unit tests + integration test (20s backoff bypassed)

title: Shared accounts: client identity and confirmed takeover
description:
Accident protection when several people use one remote account (DESIGN §4.5).

- Client identity `<local user>@<local hostname>`, overridable with
  `ACS_IDENTITY`, sent in HELLO; the master records attached and creator
  identities.
- Cross-identity attach gets BUSY{identity, since}; the client asks
  `take over? [y/N]` on the terminal, retries HELLO with `force` on yes;
  without a terminal it fails; `--force` skips the question.
- Same identity takes over silently (own dropped connection, own second
  terminal).

Tests (harness): same identity silent; different identity BUSY; force
takes over; non-tty without `--force` fails.
close_reason: Client identity (ACS_IDENTITY or user@host) in HELLO; BUSY answered with a cooked-mode [y/N] prompt naming who and since when, --force skips, non-tty declines; same identity silent takeover; ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION; 5 pty tests

title: Multi-user integration tests in a Linux container
description:
Prove isolation between Unix accounts (DESIGN §4.5, §9.1) in a Linux
container with two users (docker/podman; the macOS host cannot switch uids
without root).

- Another user's pre-created `/tmp/acs-<uid>` (squatted, and symlinked) is
  refused.
- A connection from another uid to a master's socket is dropped.
- Two users' `main` sessions are independent.
- The whole `cargo test` suite also runs on Linux musl in the container.

Acceptance: one script (`scripts/test_linux.sh`) runs it end to end.
close_reason: tests/multiuser.rs (squatted dir, symlinked dir, foreign peer uid dropped by master, independent per-user main) + scripts/test_linux.sh running the full suite on Linux musl and the multi-user tests as root with alice/bob; all pass. The Linux run found and fixed a master backpressure stall and a replaced-binary spawn failure.

title: Frame codec, message types and ACS-READY marker
description:
Implement the wire protocol of DESIGN §5.1 in `proto.rs`.

- Frame: `type u8 | len u32 BE | payload`. Hard maximum frame length
  (e.g. 1 MiB) rejected as a protocol error.
- Incremental decoder that accepts arbitrary read boundaries.
- All message types: HELLO (incl. client identity, `force`, TERM, COLORTERM,
  size, optional resume{instance, offset}), WELCOME (resumed/gap/fresh,
  created), BUSY, DATA (u64 offset), INPUT (u64 seq), ACK, RESIZE, PING/PONG,
  DETACH, KILL, EXIT, TAKEOVER, STATUS/STATUS_REPLY, ERROR.
- `PROTO_VERSION` constant; the `ACS-READY <proto>\n` marker and the
  `ACS-NEED <os> <arch>` line (DESIGN §3, §8): emit and a scanner that
  discards arbitrary preceding noise.

Tests: round-trip every message; decode with the input split at every byte
boundary; oversize and unknown-type frames error; marker found after
shell-rc noise and across split reads.
close_reason: proto.rs: frames, all message types, incremental decoder, ACS-READY/ACS-NEED scanner; 9 unit tests

title: Payload set: format, ELF trailer and Mach-O embed
description:
Carry slim remote binaries inside a complete binary (DESIGN §8.1).

- Payload set format: index of (target triple, compressed size, SHA-256,
  gzip bytes).
- ELF: trailer `[slim][P entries][index][magic + index offset]`, read back
  through `current_exe()`; writer used by xtask and by `_install --finish`.
- Mach-O: `embed-payloads` cargo feature using `include_bytes!` of a path
  supplied at build time.
- API: `own_target()`, `is_complete()`, `payload_for(target)`.

Tests: build a synthetic trailer and read it back; truncated or corrupt
trailer means slim, never a crash.
close_reason: payload.rs: blob format (gz entries + index + footer), build/parse, ELF trailer via current_exe, embed-payloads feature via include_bytes (build.rs ACS_PAYLOADS_FILE), own target (build.rs ACS_TARGET), uname->target map; dependency-free sha256.rs with FIPS vectors; corrupt/truncated input never panics

title: Remote self-install: ACS-NEED, versioned install, _install --finish
description:
Install `acs` on a remote on first contact (DESIGN §8, §8.1, §4.5).

- On `ACS-NEED <os> <arch>` map to a target. Case 1 (own ELF target):
  stream own file with `cat`. Case 2 (Linux target in P): stream gz(slim_r)
  to `gzip -dc > ~/.local/share/acs/<v>/acs.new.<token>`, then run
  `acs.new.<token> _install --finish --sha256 <digest>` with P on stdin,
  which appends the trailer, verifies the digest, renames to `acs`, and
  repoints `~/.local/bin/acs` (temp symlink + rename). Case 3 (macOS other
  arch): clear manual-install message.
- Random token per install so concurrent installs converge; missing `gzip`
  gives a clear error; side calls keep the user's ssh multiplexing; redial
  after install.

Tests (harness, local "remote" with temp HOME): install from slim fails
cleanly with the `cargo xtask dist` hint; complete binary installs and the
installed copy is byte-identical to the dist output for that target;
concurrent same-version installs converge; two versions coexist and each
serves its own client.
close_reason: install.rs: plan (self-copy for own target; gzip'd slim + payload blob for other Linux targets; clear errors otherwise), side calls, _install --finish (sha256 check, new file since running exe is ETXTBSY, atomic rename, ~/.local/bin symlink swap), once per run; --version lists installable targets; 6 integration tests incl. payload path via fake uname, concurrent installs, corrupt upload; verified dist binaries in docker

title: Prune unused remote versions
description:
Housekeeping from DESIGN §8: `_proxy` touches its version directory on
start; version directories untouched for 30 days with no running master of
that version (per STATUS) are removed at the next proxy start.

Tests: old unused version pruned; old version with a live master kept;
current version never pruned.

title: Resume buffers: output ring with u64 offsets and input ack tracking
description:
Data structures behind lossless resume (DESIGN §4.2, §5.2).

- Output ring: append bytes, monotonically increasing u64 offsets,
  configurable capacity (default 1 MiB); `read_from(offset)` returns
  data / Gap (overwritten) / Future (invalid). Tracks the unsent watermark of
  the attached client so the master can apply backpressure.
- Input tracking: client-side queue of sent-but-unacked bytes (push, ack up
  to seq, iterate for resend); master-side dedupe that writes only the part
  of a resent INPUT beyond the last written seq.

Tests: wrap-around; gap detection exactly at the boundary; resend that
partially overlaps what the master already wrote is not duplicated.

title: Command-key detector: Ctrl-] Ctrl-] then d (detach) / x (exit)
description:
Pure state machine for command mode (DESIGN §6.1-6.3), fed stdin bytes plus
an injected clock; outputs bytes to forward, actions (Detach, Exit) and the
next deadline.

- First Ctrl-] held up to 400 ms; a lone Ctrl-] or Ctrl-] + other key is
  forwarded as typed. Ctrl-] Ctrl-] within the window enters command mode;
  `d` / `x` act; any other key, or 2 s of nothing, forwards all held bytes.
- Recognise all encodings: legacy `0x1D`; kitty `CSI 93;5u` including event
  types `:1/:2/:3`; modifyOtherKeys `CSI 27;5;93~`. Consume whole escape
  sequences (never match inside one); buffer sequences split across reads;
  release events follow their press (forwarded or swallowed together).
- Bracketed paste (`CSI 200~` ... `CSI 201~`) passes through untouched.
- Escape key and window configurable (`ACS_ESCAPE_TIMEOUT_MS`).

Tests: table-driven `(bytes, timings) -> (forwarded, action)` covering every
rule above, including a pasted `^]^]d` and a terminal reply (`ESC`-prefixed)
arriving while a Ctrl-] is held.
close_reason: keys.rs Detector: legacy/kitty/modifyOtherKeys, releases, split reads, bracketed paste, passive replies/mouse, timeouts, configurable key; 20 table tests

title: Terminal mode observer and reset-on-detach sequences
description:
Passive scanner over the output stream that records which terminal modes the
remote program has turned on, and produces the matching resets for detach,
exit, or an abandoned reconnect (DESIGN §6.4). It must never modify, delay or
reorder the stream.

Modes: mouse (1000/1002/1003/1006/1015), bracketed paste (2004), alternate
screen (47/1047/1049), cursor visibility (25), focus events (1004), kitty
keyboard stack (`CSI > flags u` / `CSI < u`), modifyOtherKeys (`CSI > 4;N m`).

Tests: each sequence split at every byte boundary; reset output matches the
recorded state and is empty when nothing was set.

title: Session names and per-uid socket directory
description:
Everything about where sessions live (DESIGN §4.1, §4.4, §4.5).

- Name validation `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; default `main` or `$ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION`.
- Directory: `$ACS_SOCKET_DIR` or `/tmp/acs-<getuid()>` (never `$USER`,
  never `$TMPDIR`). Create `0700`; on existing path `lstat`: must be a real
  directory, not a symlink, owned by our uid, mode `0700` — else refuse with
  an error naming the owner and suggesting `ACS_SOCKET_DIR`.
- `sun_path` length check with a clear error.
- `flock` helpers for the per-session creation lock and the directory lock
  used by `--new` to pick the lowest free number.

Tests: symlinked dir refused; wrong mode refused; ownership check via an
injectable stat; too-long path; `--new` numbering with gaps and under
concurrent callers.

title: ssh command builder, option passthrough and remote prelude
description:
Build every ssh invocation (DESIGN §3, §7.1, §8).

- Session calls: transport options first (`-T -e none -o ControlMaster=no
  -o ControlPath=none -o ServerAliveInterval=0`), then the user's `-i`, `-p`,
  `-J`, `-F`, `-o` in the order given, then `[user@]host`, then the remote
  command. Side calls (`--list`, install) omit the transport options so they
  keep the user's multiplexing.
- ssh binary from `--ssh` / `ACS_SSH`, default `ssh` on PATH.
- Hidden `--transport-cmd <cmd>` that replaces ssh with a local command, for
  the integration harness (DESIGN §9.1).
- Remote prelude (POSIX sh) with the client version baked in: try
  `~/.local/share/acs/<v>/acs` then `/usr/local/lib/acs/<v>/acs`, `exec
  _proxy <session> <mode>`, else print `ACS-NEED $(uname -s) $(uname -m)`.
  Everything interpolated is shell-quoted (`-- command...` args are
  arbitrary).

Tests: argv snapshots for session vs side calls; precedence (a user
`-o ControlMaster=auto` comes after ours); quoting of hostile command args.
close_reason: ssh.rs: Transport argv (transport opts first for session calls, side calls keep multiplexing, user -i/-p/-J/-F/-o in order, -- before destination, ACS_SSH, --transport-cmd hook), sh_quote, versioned prelude run under sh -c; WELCOME carries session name; 7 tests incl. executing the prelude

title: Command-line parsing (dsh-compatible)
description:
`acs [ssh options] [user@]<host> [session] [-l|--list] [--new]
[--no-reconnect] [--force] [-v] [-- command...]` with `lexopt` (DESIGN §4.4,
§7, §7.1).

- `-r` accepted and ignored (reconnect is the default); `-l` is `--list`;
  ssh's `-l <login>` rejected with a hint to use `user@host` or
  `-o User=`.
- Invalid combinations rejected: `--list` with a session or `--new`;
  `--new` with a session name.
- `ACS_DEFAULT_SESSION` resolves the default session name.

Tests: table of argv -> parsed config / error message, including every
`dsh` invocation form.
